about: A small, witty take on the Colossal Cave. A barrow leads to a cavern. Turning on the lamp summons a Wizard whose spells conjure things (a sphere, a grue) that the room admits were never really there.

done.why: I left after a short sample of nine turns. I had seen the opening and the Wizard's trick and stopped before exploring further.

moments.note: The lantern description says it looks like it has been through one adventure already.
Turning on the lamp made the Wizard appear, and he cast Fantasize.
Trying to take the conjured sphere got a witty refusal, with the room described as embarrassed.
A grue was listed in the room, and the room then settled down. I couldn't tell whether it was real or conjured.

wished: Ask the Wizard something, or follow him.
Examine the grue to see whether it was a conjured thing too.

lines.line: It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: Personifies the room and makes a refusal funny.

lines.line: The room, which had been looking a little odd round the edges, settles down and is only a room.
lines.why: A good, quiet way to show the conjuring wearing off.

fun.why: The Wizard's conjuring and the room's wry replies were charming.

engagement.why: I wanted to see what the Wizard would conjure next.

difficulty.why: I met no puzzles in this short sample.

interestingness.why: It plays on Colossal Cave while adding illusions that vanish.

prose.why: The prose is witty and well turned. The plain room descriptions are borrowed or flat by comparison.
